question: What are customers contacting us about most, and what is changing?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Customers contact the bank mostly about money taken or money held — fraud, service failures and account restrictions — and across two years that mix has barely moved.**

Across all 5,425 contacts in the index, unauthorized activity or fraud is the single biggest reason, on 1,337 contacts (24.6%), followed by customer service experience (1,031 contacts, 19.0%) and terms, information or communication (811 contacts, 14.9%). Inside the real complaint corpus on its own — 4,425 written CFPB complaints about the bank, July 2024 to June 2026 — fraud is more concentrated still at 28.4% (1,257 complaints), and funds holds or account restrictions come third at 13.6% (601 complaints).

What is changing is, mostly, not much. Of the five largest complaint reasons, covering 2,893 complaints, four test flat over the 24 months. Only fees and charges has a statistically detectable direction and it points down (t = -2.11): 6.5% of complaints overall, 9.3% in July 2024 against 7.0% in June 2026. Customer service experience is the one to watch: its share of monthly complaints ran at 16.2% in the first month and 28.0% in the last, but month-to-month noise is wide enough that the trend test still reads flat (t = 0.94).

At theme level, only one of nine testable themes is flagged as emerging at the as-of week: promised callbacks or follow-ups that never happen, with 6 complaints in the most recent weeks against 1.8 expected (z = 2.79). It is a thin signal that does not survive an eight-week re-test, but it sits directly underneath the second-biggest contact reason.

The shape of the demand matters as much as the topic. 38.8% of contacts ask for a refund or a reversal and 25.4% ask for an error to be fixed, and 74.2% are recorded as unresolved.

caveats: The index holds two different corpora and every unfiltered number mixes them: 4,425 real written CFPB complaints about one bank (July 2024 to June 2026) and 1,000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations from September 2023 only. The reason mix differs sharply between them, so the combined ranking is partly a mix effect: terms, information or communication is 14.9% of all contacts but only 6.2% of complaints.
All trend and emerging findings here are scoped to the CFPB complaints, because the synthetic conversation set covers a single month and gives no baseline to measure change against.
A complaint corpus is self-selected and regulator-mediated. It measures what people escalate, not overall contact volume or overall customer satisfaction.

The emerging callback theme rests on 6 complaints in the recent weeks and does not stay flagged when the same test is run over eight weeks, so it is a watch item rather than a trend. Contact reasons are also multi-label, so shares do not sum to 100%.
followups: Is the rise in customer service experience complaints real? Compare the last six months against the prior six months within the CFPB corpus only.
Within fraud, which specific failure is growing fastest: claims denied, provisional credit never issued, or no callback after the claim was filed?
